symptoms: Concentric dark brown rings ('target board' spots) on older lower leaves
Yellow halos surrounding brown necrotic spots
Premature leaf drop starting from bottom of plant upward
Dark, sunken, leathery cankers on stems and fruit attachment points
prevention: Maintain 2-3 year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (avoid potato, brinjal, chili)
Ensure proper plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) for good air circulation
Use drip irrigation or furrow watering to avoid wetting foliage
Stake plants and mulch soil surface to prevent soil splash onto lower leaves
ipm_measures: Prune and burn/bury severely infected lower leaves immediately
Apply bio-fungicides like Trichoderma viride or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5g/L as preventive spray
Spray neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) or neem oil (3ml/L) at first sign of symptoms
safe_input_guidance: If disease exceeds 5% leaf area, apply Mancozeb 75% WP @ 2.5g/L or Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L
For severe infections, spray Azoxystrobin 18.2% + Difenoconazole 11.4% SC @ 1ml/L
Adhere strictly to a 7-10 day waiting/pre-harvest interval (PHI) and wear protective gear
Early Blight.when_to_contact_expert: Contact the local KVK or extension officer if more than 20% foliage is affected, stem lesions appear on young seedlings, or if standard fungicide sprays show no response within 5 days.

symptoms: Large, irregular water-soaked pale-green to dark-brown lesions on leaves
White fungal downy growth on undersides of leaves during cool, humid morning hours
Rapidly turning brown, brittle, and necrotic within 48-72 hours
Greasy dark-brown blotches on green fruit turning rot
prevention: Avoid planting downwind of old tomato/potato fields
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; water only at root zone early in morning
Select certified disease-free transplants and resistant varieties (e.g., Arka Rakshak, Kashi Adarsh)
Destroy volunteer tomato and potato plants around the field perimeter
ipm_measures: Eradicate and bag infected plants immediately to prevent airborne spore dissemination
Ensure optimal field drainage to avoid standing water after rains
Spray copper oxychloride (COC 50% WP @ 3g/L) during overcast, high-humidity weather forecasts
safe_input_guidance: Upon confirmed detection, spray Cymoxanil 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2.5g/L or Metalaxyl 8% + Mancozeb 64% WP @ 2g/L
Rotate chemical modes of action (FRAC codes) to prevent fungicide resistance
Observe 10-14 days pre-harvest interval before harvesting fruits
Late Blight.when_to_contact_expert: CRITICAL: Late Blight can destroy an entire field within 3-5 days. Contact the Taluka Agriculture Officer or KVK extension specialist IMMEDIATELY upon first identification.

symptoms: Pale green or yellowish spots on upper leaf surfaces with indistinct margins
Olive-green to brown velvety fungal patches on lower leaf surfaces directly beneath yellow spots
Infected leaves curl, wither, and drop prematurely in high humidity conditions
prevention: Maximize ventilation and airflow through pruning and wider row spacing
Avoid excess relative humidity (>85%) inside polyhouses or dense canopies
Clean and sterilize trellising stakes and pruning shears regularly
ipm_measures: Remove suckers and lower senescent leaves to improve light penetration and air movement
Spray bio-formulation of Bacillus subtilis @ 5ml/L at early vegetative stage
safe_input_guidance: Apply Copper hydroxide 77% WP @ 2g/L or Carbendazim 50% WP @ 1g/L at initial symptom onset
Ensure thorough coverage of both upper and lower leaf surfaces during spraying
Leaf Mold.when_to_contact_expert: Contact extension worker if mold spreads to upper canopy leaves during flowering stage.

symptoms: Numerous small (1.5-3mm), circular spots with dark brown borders and grayish-white centers
Tiny black specks (pycnidia fruiting bodies) visible in the center of mature spots
Severe leaf yellowing and blighting from ground level upward, exposing fruit to sunscald
prevention: Practice strict 3-year crop rotation away from solanaceous species
Deep summer ploughing to bury crop residues harboring overwintering fungal spores
Mulch beds with straw or black plastic to create a barrier against soil splash
ipm_measures: Hand-pick and destroy initial infected leaves before rain/irrigation events
Disinfect field tools and avoid working in wet fields to prevent spore transfer
safe_input_guidance: Spray Chlorothalonil 75% WP @ 2g/L or Zineb 75% WP @ 2g/L on 7-10 day intervals
Use protective gloves and face mask during chemical application
Septoria Leaf Spot.when_to_contact_expert: Consult your agricultural extension worker if defoliation exceeds 15% before fruit set.

symptoms: Small (2-3mm), water-soaked, dark brown to black angular lesions on leaves
Lesions often have greasy texture and may coalesce causing leaf tearing and shot-holes
Scabby, rough, raised dark-brown spots with white halos on green fruit
prevention: Use certified disease-free, hot-water treated seeds (50°C for 25 minutes)
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation; disinfect nursery trays and tools with 1% sodium hypochlorite
Do not handle plants when foliage is wet
ipm_measures: Remove and destroy symptomatic seedlings before field transplanting
Foliar spray with Streptocycline @ 0.5g/10L water combined with Copper Oxychloride @ 25g/10L
safe_input_guidance: Apply Copper hydroxide 53.8% DF @ 1.5g/L mixed with Mancozeb @ 2g/L for synergy
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces succulent tissue prone to bacterial entry
Bacterial Spot.when_to_contact_expert: Contact KVK plant pathologist if fruit spots appear across more than 10% of plants.

symptoms: Upward curling and cupping of leaf margins with marked chlorosis (yellowing)
Severe plant stunting, shortened internodes, and bushy upright growth habit
Flower abortion and dramatically reduced fruit set; newly formed fruits remain small
prevention: Use 40-50 mesh insect-proof nets in nurseries to prevent whitefly vector entry
Plant barrier crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet around tomato fields
Use TYLCV-tolerant hybrid cultivars (e.g., US-440, To-1057, Abhinav)
ipm_measures: Install yellow sticky traps @ 20-25 traps per acre to monitor and capture whiteflies (Bemisia tabaci)
Spray Neem Oil (10,000 ppm) @ 2ml/L or Lecanicillium lecanii @ 5g/L targeting undersides of leaves
Rogue out and destroy infected viral plants immediately upon sighting
safe_input_guidance: For vector control during early stages: Spray Acetamiprid 20% SP @ 0.5g/L or Thiamethoxam 25% WG @ 0.3g/L or Diafenthiuron 50% WP @ 1g/L
Rotate insecticides across distinct IRAC classes to avoid whitefly insecticide resistance
Yellow Leaf Curl Virus.when_to_contact_expert: Inform extension staff if whitefly population exceeds 5 adults per leaf or viral stunting affects >5% of the plot within 30 days of transplanting.

symptoms: Vibrant green leaves with uniform coloration and no necrotic spots or chlorosis
Sturdy stem structure and vigorous vegetative/reproductive development
Normal leaf morphology without cupping, mottling, or fungal spore growth
prevention: Maintain regular crop scouting every 3-4 days, inspecting leaf undersides and new shoots
Ensure balanced N-P-K nutrient application along with micronutrients (Zinc, Boron, Calcium)
Maintain consistent soil moisture through scheduled drip irrigation
ipm_measures: Keep field borders free from weeds that could serve as alternative viral or pest reservoirs
Deploy monitoring pheromone traps (for Tomato Pinworm / Fruit borer) @ 5 traps/acre
safe_input_guidance: No chemical fungicides or bactericides required
Apply prophylactic biostimulant or seaweed extract foliar spray for enhanced plant vigor
Healthy.when_to_contact_expert: Continue standard crop management. Consult your local extension worker during scheduled routine village visits or if any unexpected symptoms emerge.
